name: Run My AI Biz
description:
Comprehensive Business Description
Run My AI Business, operated by Jacqui Abrams and supported by the Run My AI Biz newsletter on Substack, is an AI-focused educational publishing and independent reseller business. It helps aspiring entrepreneurs, solopreneurs, digital product creators, and small business owners explore how artificial intelligence can support the creation, launch, and ongoing management of online businesses. Its content emphasizes practical applications, approachable explanations, and conversational workflows that allow users to direct AI in everyday language without needing to learn coding.

The business addresses a common challenge for entrepreneurs: bringing together the many pieces needed to turn an idea into a functioning business. Its educational focus spans business planning, AI-assisted product development, digital product creation, sales copy, sales pages, lead magnets, sales funnels, email follow-up, scheduling, and recurring operational tasks. Rather than presenting these as disconnected activities, Run My AI Business explores how specialized AI assistants can work together around the owner’s business goals.

Educational Content and Newsletter
Run My AI Biz is the business’s weekly Substack newsletter. It provides sourced AI tool comparisons, pricing breakdowns, explanations of AI’s development, step-by-step example businesses, and quick-start ideas. Its purpose is to help readers understand what different tools do, how they fit into an online business, and how to move from researching possibilities to taking practical action. The supplied business description lists a free starting option and a paid subscription of $9 per month for access to full weekly issues.

Topics include AI for entrepreneurs, online business automation, digital products, lead generation, sales funnels, and ongoing business management. Educational examples explore how an idea can become an offer, how marketing materials can support that offer, and how workflows can be adapted to different audiences and selling platforms.

The newsletter complements, but remains separate from, the external mastermind Jacqui promotes. It provides ongoing educational content, while the mastermind offers demonstrations, business examples, and resources for developing specialized AI assistants.

AI Business Mastermind and 38-Bot Resource Library
As an independent reseller, Jacqui promotes a separate AI business mastermind featuring three entrepreneurs who share examples of their business workflows and AI assistants. An accompanying resource, The 38 Bot Empire, documents 38 bot examples covering business planning, research, content production, marketing, sales, website development, and operations. These examples illustrate how specialized assistants can support different functions within one business or provide starting points for exploring several business models.

A central feature is access to customizable master prompts—the written instructions that define an assistant’s role, responsibilities, workflow, and approval requirements. Participants can adapt these instructions to their own niche, audience, products, brand voice, and objectives rather than developing every workflow from scratch. Many prompts appear directly in the guide; others are referenced in separate “Private Stash” materials or supporting files. The collection is therefore a library of adaptable bot blueprints and resources, rather than 38 identical, independently functioning software products.

Business Applications and Use Cases
The resource library includes examples across several business functions:

Business planning and coordination: chief-of-staff assistants, business idea evaluation, opportunity research, project tracking, and coordination between specialized bots.

Newsletter publishing and growth: topic research, issue drafting, local and paid newsletters, subscriber acquisition strategies, and local sponsorship prospecting.

Digital products and education: course planning, presentation development, lesson scripts, video creation, video editing, and product launch preparation.

Affiliate marketing and sales funnels: offer research, lead magnets, opt-in pages, bridge pages, email sequences, advertising drafts, and campaign planning.

Website and software development: local business websites, professional directories, hosting workflows, custom software projects, and search engine optimization.

Social media and communities: Facebook content, X posts and threads, newsletter repurposing, and content development for paid communities.

Marketing strategy and conversion: competitor research, customer research, offer positioning, landing-page analysis, and webinar development.

Business administration: billing monitoring, overdue-payment reminders, first-line support workflows, and server-health reporting.

Owners can select individual assistants for specific needs or combine several into a coordinated process. For example, an opportunity-research bot could identify a topic, a course-building bot could develop educational materials, a video bot could support production, and a launch bot could help prepare the sales funnel. Other combinations could support a local newsletter, website service, professional directory, or affiliate marketing project. These are possible applications—not a claim that every bot represents a separate profitable business.

Customization, Coordination, and Human Oversight
The approach emphasizes adapting workflows to the user’s circumstances. Participants supply their business context, review drafts, request changes, and refine instructions over time. A chief-of-staff-style assistant can act as the main point of contact, helping organize projects and route tasks to other specialized bots.

Human-directed automation is a recurring principle. The guide instructs users to retain safeguards requiring approval before bots send messages, publish content, spend money, or sign up for services. Individual workflows also include review checkpoints, secure account connections, source verification, and restrictions on inventing statistics, proof, or income claims. Successful execution depends on the underlying AI platform, integrations, permissions, and supporting services—not on a prompt alone.

Although the collection supports many possible projects, its recommended starting approach is focused: identify relevant workflows, build one assistant, use it, and then expand. This allows owners to develop manageable systems before attempting to coordinate multiple projects or businesses.

Audience and Business Model
Run My AI Business serves first-time entrepreneurs, professionals developing side businesses, digital product creators, and existing business owners seeking to reduce repetitive work. Its messaging particularly addresses people who feel overwhelmed by technical instructions, disconnected software, or the number of tasks involved in launching and maintaining an online business.

The business combines subscription-based educational publishing with independent resale of the external mastermind. Jacqui’s role is to introduce and promote the program, explain potential applications, and share her perspective as a user and reseller. She earns commissions through program referrals but is not the creator of the promoted AI technology or one of the mastermind’s presenters.

Positioning and Value Proposition
Run My AI Business brings together accessible AI education and an introduction to customizable business-automation resources. Its central value proposition is helping people move beyond isolated chatbot questions toward repeatable, task-specific workflows that support business creation and ongoing operations.

The newsletter provides continuing education and practical ideas, while the mastermind’s bot resources offer examples and adaptable instructions. Together, these can help owners explore a venture, strengthen an existing operation, or coordinate several related projects while retaining control over decisions, spending, and publication.

The business presents these applications as educational opportunities rather than guaranteed outcomes. The bot guide itself distinguishes some demonstrated workflows from experimental or not-yet-used examples, so the collection should not be portrayed as 38 proven income-producing businesses.

Business Creation and Launch
AI-powered online business creation
Explore how AI can help turn an initial idea into a structured online business concept. This includes researching an audience, evaluating potential offers, developing products, preparing marketing materials, and organizing the steps needed to launch. The emphasis is on adapting AI tools and prompts to the owner’s goals rather than following a single business model.

Business launch automation and AI business launch tools
Learn how AI-assisted workflows can support product launches, including sales pages, checkout and delivery setup, upsells, downsells, thank-you pages, and promotional copy. The mastermind’s resource guide includes a launch-bot example designed to learn a platform’s setup process and help repeat it, with review before anything goes live.

AI for startups and AI-powered entrepreneurship
Use AI to support the early work of entrepreneurship: researching opportunities, comparing competitors, clarifying customer needs, developing an offer, and organizing next steps. The resource library includes opportunity-research and business-brainstorming assistants that provide starting points for evaluating ideas before committing significant resources.

AI for entrepreneurs and digital business owners
Explore practical ways to incorporate AI into an existing business or a new venture. This area connects business strategy with day-to-day execution, helping owners identify which tasks need their judgment and which could be supported by a specialized assistant.

Product Development and Digital Products
AI-assisted product development and AI product development tools
Learn how to use AI to research product opportunities, organize an idea, outline its features or content, and produce drafts for review. Relevant examples in the bot library include course development, software creation, business idea evaluation, and offer positioning.

AI digital product creation and AI for digital product creators
Explore workflows for creating educational and informational products, including course outlines, slide presentations, lesson scripts, videos, and supporting materials. The guide shows how a course-building assistant can work alongside research, video-production, and launch assistants to support different stages of product development.

How to create and sell digital products with AI
Connect product creation with the work needed to bring an offer to market. This includes defining the audience, developing the product, preparing sales copy, building a funnel, and planning promotional content. The goal is to understand the whole process rather than treating AI-generated content as a finished business.

Lead Generation, Funnels, and Marketing
AI lead magnet creation
Learn how AI can help develop useful introductory resources that encourage prospective customers to join an email list. Examples in the guide include a local activities PDF and an affiliate-related checklist, alongside the pages and follow-up materials that support them.

AI sales funnels
Explore how to connect an offer with a sequence of customer-facing materials, such as an opt-in page, lead magnet, bridge page, thank-you page, and email follow-up. The Affiliate Pro example illustrates how these components can be developed together and tailored to a selected niche and offer.

AI-powered lead generation
Use AI-assisted research to identify potential customers, sponsors, or business partners and prepare relevant outreach for review. The library includes examples involving YouTube prospect research, local businesses needing websites, and potential sponsors for local newsletters. The focus is on researched prospects and appropriate outreach—not guaranteed leads or sales.

AI marketing automation
Explore repeatable workflows for drafting email sequences, preparing social media content, repurposing newsletters, developing advertising materials, and organizing campaigns. The guide includes examples for Facebook, X, newsletters, and affiliate promotions, with approval requirements before relevant publishing or spending actions.

AI tools for business growth
Learn how AI can support subscriber acquisition ideas, competitor research, offer positioning, website reviews, and conversion-focused improvements. Examples include newsletter growth assistants, a demand-research assistant, and a landing-page review assistant that prioritizes suggested changes. These tools support testing and decision-making rather than guaranteeing growth.

Business Operations and Automation
AI workflow automation and AI business automation
Identify repeatable processes and turn them into structured instructions for specialized assistants. Examples include recurring research briefs, newsletter drafts, content repurposing, project updates, and administrative checks. The resource guide demonstrates how several assistants can be coordinated through a chief-of-staff-style bot.

Online business automation
Explore how AI can support connected activities across publishing, digital products, affiliate marketing, websites, and online communities. Rather than automating a single isolated task, the aim is to organize a sequence of tasks with clear inputs, review points, and owner approval.

AI-powered business management and AI business systems
Learn how to organize projects, track progress, identify stalled work, and receive concise operational updates. The library’s chief-of-staff examples coordinate tasks and assistants, while its hosting-and-billing example covers payment monitoring, support workflows, and server-health reporting.

Automating repetitive business tasks
Identify recurring work that could be delegated to an AI-assisted workflow, such as collecting research, drafting routine content, checking links, organizing prospect information, and preparing payment reminders. The purpose is to reduce repeated manual effort while keeping review and exception-handling responsibilities clear.

AI productivity tools for entrepreneurs
Explore tools and prompts that help owners spend less time gathering information and preparing first drafts. The bot collection includes scheduled research, consolidated reports, daily updates, and content-production workflows that can provide a more organized starting point for the owner’s work.

How to automate a small business
Learn to start with a specific operational problem rather than attempting to automate everything at once. The guide recommends choosing relevant assistants, building one, using it, and then expanding. This supports a focused approach to implementation, review, and refinement.

Support for Different Business Owners
AI for small business
Explore applications relevant to smaller operations, including website development, local marketing, customer-support drafts, billing follow-up, and identifying overlooked business opportunities. The resource library includes examples designed around local service businesses and their administrative or marketing needs.

AI for solopreneurs and running a one-person business with AI
Learn how a single owner can coordinate several specialized assistants for research, content, marketing, and administration. A chief-of-staff assistant can provide a central point of contact, but the owner still supplies direction, checks quality, connects accounts, and approves consequential actions.

Applying AI tools across multiple business projects
Explore how reusable prompts can be adapted to different brands, audiences, products, or niches. For example, similar newsletter workflows can support a local publication or a topic-focused publication, while their voice, sources, and offers remain distinct. The guide encourages focused implementation rather than launching every possible project simultaneously.

Practical Education and Customizable Tools
Practical AI education for aspiring online business owners
Provide approachable explanations of how AI-assisted business workflows operate, what setup they require, and where human judgment remains necessary. This includes understanding prompts, reviewing outputs, connecting supporting tools, and distinguishing a demonstration from a proven business outcome.

AI business tools and AI tools for digital entrepreneurs
Introduce readers to task-specific assistants and the supporting platforms needed to use them. Through the mastermind’s resource library, participants can explore customizable master prompts for different functions, with many prompts supplied in the guide and others referenced in accompanying materials.

How to use AI to run a business
Bring strategy, content creation, marketing, and administration into a coordinated approach. The emphasis is on using AI to assist with defined responsibilities while the owner retains control of business decisions. A prompt provides instructions; actual execution also requires suitable tools, permissions, integrations, and oversight.

Exploring Additional Revenue Models
How to create multiple streams of income with AI
Explore how AI-assisted workflows could support different revenue models, including digital products, paid newsletters, memberships, affiliate marketing, website services, and paid directory listings. The 38-bot collection offers examples that can be adapted to these models, either within an existing business or as separate projects. It does not establish that each bot is a standalone income stream because each user will have their own input, but it does indicate that by using several bots for multiple streams of income will generate multiple income possibilities.
